Rashi on Sotah 9b:11:1.hebrew: בעיניו מרד - ע"י עיניו מרד בבוראו:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:11:1.english: He rebelled through his eyes - Through his eyes he rebelled against his Creator.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:12:1.hebrew: כי מה' הוא - שחשק באותה אשה כדי להתגרות בפלשתים:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:12:1.english: For it was from the Lord - That he desired that woman in order to provoke the Philistines.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:14:1.hebrew: והכתיב וירד שמשון תמנתה - "וירא שם אשה מבנות פלשתים", ותיטב בעיני שמשון. ומעשה של זו שבתמנת קודם למעשה של זו שבעזה:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:14:1.english: But it is written: "And Samson went down to Timnah" - "And he saw a woman there, of the daughters of the Philistines," and she was pleasing in Samson's eyes. And the episode of this one in Timnah precedes the episode of the one in Gaza.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:14:2.hebrew: תחילת קלקולו מיהא בעזה הוה - דההיא דתמנת לאו קילקול הוא כולי האי, שלקחה לו לאשה ולא בא עליה בזנות:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:14:2.english: The beginning of his corruption, at any rate, was in Azza - For that [incident] of Timnat was not so much of a corruption, since he took her as a wife and did not come upon her in fornication.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:15:1.english: That it weakened - It uprooted [his strength], like [the expression] "stones of a mountain that were loosened/dangled."

Rashi on Sotah 9b:17:1.hebrew: מנא ידעה - הלא כמה כזבים אמר לה קודם לכן, ומצאתו שקרן:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:17:1.english: How did she know? - Surely he had told her many falsehoods before this, and she found him to be a liar.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:17:2.hebrew: נכרין דברי אמת - מתקבלין ומיושבין, ודבורים על אופניהם. ראתה שערו גדול, ולא היה שותה יין, והבינה שהדברים האחרונים שאמר לה, שבדבר הזה היה כחו גדול — אמת הן:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:17:2.english: The words of truth are recognizable - They are acceptable and make sense, and are spoken in their proper manner. She saw that his hair was long and that he did not drink wine, and she understood that the last things he had told her — that his strength lay in this matter — were true.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:18:1.english: And she pressed him - An expression of pressure and distress.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:18:2.hebrew: בשעת גמר ביאה - תאות האדם מרובה:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:18:2.english: At the time of the completion of intercourse - A person's desire is [then] greatest.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:19:1.hebrew: דברים האסורים לנזיר - משרת ענבים, כגון נזיר ששרה ענבים במים ויש בהם טעם יין, דלא נפקא מ״כל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ (במדבר ו׳:ד׳):
Rashi on Sotah 9b:19:1.english: Things forbidden to a nazirite - [This refers to] a grape steeping, such as a nazirite who soaked grapes in water and the water has the taste of wine, for this is not excluded from [the prohibition of] "anything that is made of the grapevine" (Numbers 6:4).

Rashi on Sotah 9b:1:1.hebrew: נחש הקדמוני - נתן עיניו בחוה ובא עליה, והיינו דכתיב (בראשית ג׳:י״ג) "הנחש השיאני", לשון תשמיש ונשואין הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:1:1.english: The primordial serpent - He set his eyes on Eve and had relations with her, and this is what is written (Genesis 3:13): "The serpent beguiled me [hishi'ani]" — it is a term of intercourse and marriage.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:1:2.english: They took from him - [His] upright stature.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:1:3.hebrew: יהא מלך - שלכך עשאו ערום מכל:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:1:3.english: Let him be king - For this reason He made him [the serpent] more cunning than all [the beasts].

Rashi on Sotah 9b:20:1.english: Mortar - The place where the tooth is fixed.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:20:2.english: He desired an impure matter - to marry the daughter of a foreign god.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:20:3.hebrew: בדבר טמא - לחי החמור, שאלמלא הוא היה מת בצמא:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:20:3.english: With an impure thing - the jawbone of the donkey, for had it not been [for that], he would have died of thirst.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:21:1.english: The spirit of the Lord - The spirit of prophecy that rested upon Jacob.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:22:1.english: Jingling before him - To accompany him wherever he goes.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:2:1.hebrew: אני אמרתי יהלך בקומה זקופה - מקללתו אתה למד, וכן כל אלה אתה למד מקללתן:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:2:1.english: I said he would walk upright - You learn from his curse; and so too, all of these you learn from their curses.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:1.hebrew: קין - נתן עיניו בתאומה יתירה שנולדה עם הבל, ששתי תאומות נולדו עמו. והיינו דכתיב (בראשית ד׳:ב׳) "את אחיו את הבל" — "שני אתים", שני ריבויים:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:1.english: Cain - He set his eyes on the extra twin sister who was born with Abel, for two twin sisters were born with him. And this is what is written (Genesis 4:2): "his brother, Abel" (*et achiv et Hevel*) — the two words "*et*" are "two inclusions," [indicating] two additional [births].

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:2.english: Korach - [He contended] over the priesthood, and was swallowed up.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:3.hebrew: בלעם - בממונו של בלק לקלל את ישראל, ונהרג במדין, שהלך ליטול שכר עשרים וארבעה אלף שנפלו מישראל בעצתו:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:3.english: Bilam - [He was punished] through the money of Balak, [for he went] to curse Israel; and he was killed in Midian, for he went to collect the payment for the twenty-four thousand of Israel who fell through his counsel.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:4.hebrew: דואג - אביר הרועים וגדול שבתלמידים היה, ונתקנא בדוד שראהו נבון דבר ואיש תואר ומראה פנים בהלכה, כדכתיב (שמואל א ט״ז:י״ח) הנה ראיתי בן לישי בית הלחמי וגו'. ואמר באגדה דחלק (דף צג:) דכל הפסוק הזה דואג אמרו בלשון הרע:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:4.english: Doeg - He was the "mightiest of the shepherds" and the greatest among the students, and he became jealous of David, whom he saw to be "prudent in speech" and "a man of form and comely appearance" in matters of halakha, as it is written (I Samuel 16:18): "Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, etc." And it says in the aggadic chapter of Chelek (page 93b) that this entire verse was spoken by Doeg as slander.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:5.hebrew: ואחיתופל - נתן עיניו במלוכה, כדאמר בחלק (דף קא:): "ראה אש יוצא מאמתו, וכסבור שעתיד למלוך". ומה שבידו נטלו הימנו, "לא יחצו ימיהם":
Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:5.english: And Achitophel - He set his eyes on the kingship, as stated in [chapter] Chelek (101b): "He saw fire emerging from his forearm, and he thought that he was destined to reign." And what he already had was taken from him, [as it says:] "They shall not live out half their days."

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:6.english: Gechazi - [He set his eyes] on the money of Naaman, and was afflicted with tzara'at.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:7.english: And Adonijah - [sought to take] Abishag, and was killed.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:8.hebrew: ועוזיה - בכהונה, והצרעת זרחה על מצחו (דברי הימים ב כ״ו:י״ט):
Rashi on Sotah 9b:3:8.english: And Uzziah - [he was haughty] with regard to the priesthood, and the leprosy broke out on his forehead (II Chronicles 26:19).

Rashi on Sotah 9b:5:1.hebrew: כי לייט כו' - וקללה היא תחלת הפורענות:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:5:1.english: When he curses, etc. - And a curse is the beginning of punishment.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:5:2.hebrew: מיהו כי בדקי מיא כי אורחייהו בדקי - שבמעיים נכנסו תחילה, ומקלקלות אותן, ואח"כ נופלות לירך:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:5:2.english: But when they examine the water, they examine it in the usual way - For [the waters] first enter the intestines and damage them, and afterward they fall to the thigh.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:5:3.hebrew: שלא להוציא לעז - שיאמרו: לא עשו כסדר האלה, ואין פורענות זו על ידן:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:5:3.english: So as not to give rise to a slander - So that they would not say: They did not do [it] in the order of the curse, and this punishment does not come about through them.

Rashi on Sotah 9b:6:1.english: Samson followed his eyes - As we derive below:

Rashi on Sotah 9b:7:1.hebrew: על עשר פלגשי אביו - כדכתיב בספר שמואל (ב טו) ויעזוב עשר נשים פלגשים לשמור הבית:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:7:1.english: Upon his father's ten concubines - As it is written in the book of Samuel (II 15): "And [the king] left ten women, concubines, to keep the house."

Rashi on Sotah 9b:7:3.hebrew: לב אביו ולב ב"ד - דכתיב (שם) "אלכה נא ואשלמה את נדרי" וגו'. וכתיב "את אבשלום הלכו מאתים איש קרואים והולכים לתומם". ואמרינן בסוטה דירושלמי: קרואים — מדוד, שעל ידי מצות דוד הלכו עמו. אמר לו: כתוב לי שילכו עמי אותן שנים שאבחר. וכתב לו, והיה מראה חותמו של דוד לשנים, והולכים אחריו, וכן לשנים אחרים, עד שכינס מאתים. וכולן ראשי סנהדראות. הרי לב אביו ולב ב"ד. ולב אנשי ישראל, דכתיב "בקרב איש להשתחוות" וגו', וכתיב "מי ישימני שופט בארץ", וכתיב "ויגנוב אבשלום את לב אנשי ישראל":
Rashi on Sotah 9b:7:3.english: The heart of his father and the heart of the court - For it is written (there): "Let me go, please, and pay my vow," etc. And it is written: "With Absalom went two hundred men, invited, and they went in their innocence." And we say in the Sotah [tractate] of the Jerusalem [Talmud]: "Invited" — by David, [meaning] that by David's authorization they went with him. [Absalom] said to him: Write for me that those two [men] whom I choose may go with me. And [David] wrote for him, and [Absalom] would show David's seal to two [men], and they would follow him; and so with two others, until he had assembled two hundred. And all of them were heads of Sanhedrins. Behold, [he stole] the heart of his father and the heart of the court. And [also] the heart of the men of Israel, as it is written: "when any man came near to bow down," etc., and it is written: "Who will make me judge in the land," and it is written: "And Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel."

Rashi on Sotah 9b:9:1.hebrew: ואין באחיו גדול ממנו - שהיה מלך. הרי מדה שמדד, שנקבר אביו בגדולים, ובו במדה מדדו לו, שנקבר הוא בגדולים:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:9:1.english: And among his brothers there was none greater than him - For he was a king. Behold, the measure that he measured: that his father was buried among the great [ones], and with that same measure they measured for him: that he too was buried among the great [ones].

Rashi on Sotah 9b:9:2.hebrew: מי לנו - לענין כבוד קבורה לקבר בגדולים, גדול מיוסף, שלא נתעסק בו אלא משה, שהוא גדול מישראל ואין בישראל גדול ממנו. הרי שבמדה שמדד לקבור את יוסף ע"י גדול, בה מדדו לו: שאין גדול בכבודו קבור ממשה, שלא נתעסק בו אלא הקב"ה:
Rashi on Sotah 9b:9:2.english: Who do we have - With regard to the honor of burial, to be buried among the great, [who is] greater than Joseph, in whose burial no one engaged except Moses, who is the greatest of Israel, and there is no one in Israel greater than him? Behold, with the measure by which he measured — to bury Joseph through a great person — with that [same measure] they measured for him: for there is no one buried with greater honor than Moses, in whose burial no one engaged except the Holy One, blessed be He.

Tosafot on Sotah 9b:8:1.hebrew: מרים המתינה למשה שעה אחת - לאו דוקא נקט שעה, אלא שליש שעה או רביע, דקתני בתוספתא: מדה טובה מרובה ממדת פורענות, על אחת חמש מאות. אבל קשיא לרבי: והא במרגלים נפרע מהם יום לשנה, יום לשנה — אם כן, היתה מרובה מדת פורענות ממדה טובה של מרים. ועוד, בפ"ק דחגיגה (דף ה:) דדרש רבי יוחנן: "אותי יום יום ידרושון" — שכל העוסק בתורה אפילו יום אחד, כאילו עוסק כל השנה כולה. וכן במדת פורענות כתיב (במדבר י״ד:ל״ד): "במספר הימים אשר תרתם את הארץ מ' יום" וגו' — אלמא דכי הדדי נינהו:
Tosafot on Sotah 9b:8:1.english: Miriam waited for Moses for one hour - [The Mishnah] did not necessarily mean specifically an hour, but a third of an hour or a quarter, since it is taught in the Tosefta: The measure of good is greater than the measure of punishment, by one to five hundred. But it is difficult for Rabbi: Surely in the case of the spies, they were punished one day for a year, one day for a year — so the measure of punishment was greater than the measure of good given to Miriam! Furthermore, in the first chapter of Chagigah (5b), Rabbi Yochanan expounded: "Me they seek day by day" — that whoever engages in Torah study even for one day, it is as if they engaged in it for the entire year. And similarly regarding the measure of punishment it is written (Numbers 14:34): "According to the number of the days that you spied out the land, forty days..." etc. — evidently, they are equal to one another.
